Section 4 • \(\xi\)3D

4.4 Reduction to the 1D 2PCF, \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\Delta)\)

The 1D 2PCF is obtained from \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) by evaluating it at zero transverse separation, \(\vec{r}_\perp=\vec{0}\), and not by integrating it over \(\vec{r}_\perp\) (which would give a different function of \(\Delta\), mixing pairs of points on different sightlines). To derive it, it is important to keep in mind the role of the two transverse vectors in Eq. (4.2):

  • \(\vec{x}_\perp\) is the position of the first point of the pair, i.e. the sightline on which it lies. The integral \(\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\) is the average over the positions of the pairs, and it is present in \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) for every value of \(\vec{r}_\perp\).

  • \(\vec{r}_\perp\) is the transverse separation between the two points of the pair, i.e. the argument of the 2PCF.

To avoid confusion with the 3D object, we denote the per-sightline 1D estimator, whose first argument is a position and not a separation, by \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;\Delta\right) \equiv \frac{1}{L_\Lambda-\Delta} \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b-\Delta}\! d\Lambda\; \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\, \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta\right), \qquad 0\le\Delta<L_\Lambda . \tag{4.10} \end{equation}

We then define \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\Delta)\equiv\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp}=\vec{0},\Delta)\), i.e. we keep only the pairs with zero transverse separation: both points lie on the same sightline (Fig. 9).

Step by step:

  1. At \(\vec{r}_\perp=\vec{0}\) the window becomes \(W_{\vec{0},\Delta}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)=\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}(\vec{x}_\perp)\, \mathbf{1}_{[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b]}(\Lambda+\Delta)\). Inside \(\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\) the first factor is always one, and for \(\Delta\ge0\) the second one reduces the spectral integral to \(\Lambda\in[\Lambda_a,\Lambda_b-\Delta]\).

  2. The numerator of Eq. (4.2) becomes \(\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}d^2x_\perp\int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b-\Delta}d\Lambda\; \delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda)\,\delta_j^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda+\Delta)\), where both fields are now evaluated on the same sightline \(\vec{x}_\perp\), and the denominator becomes \(|\mathcal{A}_\perp|\,(L_\Lambda-\Delta)\).

  3. Grouping the spectral integral with the factor \(1/(L_\Lambda-\Delta)\), one recognizes Eq. (4.10):

\begin{align} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\Delta\right) \;\equiv\; \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp}=\vec{0},\,\Delta\right) &= \frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}_\perp|}\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp\; \underbrace{ \frac{1}{L_\Lambda-\Delta} \int_{\Lambda_a}^{\Lambda_b-\Delta}\! d\Lambda\; \delta_i^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\, \delta_j^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda+\Delta\right) }_{\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}(\vec{x}_\perp;\Delta)} \notag\\ &= \frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}_\perp|}\int_{\mathcal{A}_\perp}\! d^2x_\perp\; \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s),\rm 1D}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp;\Delta\right). \tag{4.11} \end{align} The 1D 2PCF is therefore the per-sightline 1D estimator averaged over all the sightlines: each sightline is first correlated with itself, and the results are then averaged. The integral over \(\vec{x}_\perp\) is this average over sightlines, not an integral over transverse separations. In terms of Eq. (4.5), where the integrand does not depend on \(\varphi\) at \(r_\perp=0\), \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(r_\perp=0,\Delta)=2\pi\,\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\Delta)\).
